overview: A net-new capability that brings university-owned IP into the existing Wildfire app. Universities hold valuable IP created by professors, but professors often don't want to (or, at some schools like DSU, are career-disincentivized from) building a company around it — while the university wants companies spun out so the IP gets monetized. An IP Manager (e.g. Kirby or Peter at USD) imports/enters the university's IP into the app as ideas, associates each with the professor who created it, and — after talking to that professor — routes each piece of IP down one of THREE paths, then TRACKS how each idea is doing on its route. University IP is represented in the app simply as an 'idea' ('the research is just an idea in our world'), not a separate object type. [GAP: exact placement/section in the app not stated — PO to confirm.]
problem: [PARTIAL FROM TRANSCRIPT] Universities own strong IP that mostly sits idle: the professor who created it usually won't build a company around it (no time, and at some schools it hurts their career path), yet the university wants that IP monetized via spun-out companies. There is no way today to get university IP into the Wildfire app, associate it with its professor, and route it toward a founder, a hackathon, or a founder match. [GAP: crisp one-line problem statement not stated verbatim — PO to confirm wording.]
solution: Give a new IP Manager role (one merged role — the VP of Research is NOT a separate role) a way to bring a university's IP into the Wildfire app (import a spreadsheet of IP or add individually), keep it private by default, associate each idea with its professor, flag whether that professor wants to be a day-to-day co-founder or just a contact, and then route/publish each piece of IP down one of three paths: (1) Founder route — the professor becomes a Founder (tagged as university-IP-origin) and runs the normal Wildfire process (with a co-founder found via Founder Match); (2) Hackathon route — the IP becomes a pickable hackathon idea; (3) Founder Match route — find a founder to run with an idea the professor doesn't want to build and that isn't a good hackathon fit. The IP Manager then tracks all data associated with each idea across its route — founder-route progress through the Wildfire program, what was built at the hackathon, and how the founder match is doing — reusing the app's existing founder-tracking system as the framework. Each university is its own fully isolated organization.

roles.name: IP Manager
roles.what: New role — ONE role (the VP of Research was merged into it at the PO gate; there is no separate VPR role or tab). The person who knows and manages the university's IP (e.g. Kirby or Peter at USD; the holder may carry a VPR title like Dan or Ashley). Makes the decision to put the university's IP into the app, imports/enters IP, writes the idea summary, associates the professor, flags professor involvement (co-founder vs contact), chooses each idea's route after talking to the professor, publishes / selects IP for hackathons, and TRACKS all data associated with each idea across all three routes: founder-route progress through the Wildfire program, what was built at the hackathon, and how the founder match / matched founder is doing — modeled on the app's existing founder-tracking system. Role title in the app is 'IP Manager' regardless of the person's university title.
roles.access: Edit (own university's IP only — other universities are invisible)

roles.name: Professor (idea owner) = Founder
roles.what: The professor who created the IP. Even though the university owns the IP, the professor owns all the knowledge of the idea. In the app they carry the existing Founder tag (no separate 'professor' role) PLUS a special analytics tag marking that this founder originated from a university IP idea (confirmed at gate). Two profiles: (a) wants to be a hands-on co-founder, (b) wants to hand it off with minimal involvement and just be a contact. Could also be a Mentor, but that's unlikely.

roles.name: Co-founder (via Founder Match)
roles.what: A student or a Wildfire Network member matched to a professor's idea through the existing Founder Match. Becomes the second founder in the company (two founders, as set up today).

roles.name: Wildfire Admin / Super Admin
roles.what: Existing WFL staff role. [GAP: not discussed in this meeting] — grounding implies WFL staff must provision each university as an organization and assign its IP Manager. Surfaced as a recommendation (REC-2), not a confirmed decision.

decisions.title: Three routes for each piece of IP
decisions.detail: After the IP Manager talks to the professor, each piece of IP goes down ONE of three paths: (1) Founder — professor becomes a Founder and runs the normal Wildfire process; (2) Hackathon — becomes a pickable hackathon idea; (3) Founder Match — find a founder for an idea the professor won't build and that isn't a good hackathon fit.

decisions.title: ONE role: VP of Research merged into IP Manager
decisions.detail: PO gate decision (2026-07-02): the VPR is NOT a separate role or tab in the app. The IP Manager is the single university-side role — the decision to put IP in, the inserting/importing, routing, publishing, and tracking all live with the IP Manager. The role-holder may carry a VPR title at their university.

decisions.title: IP Manager tracks every idea across all three routes
decisions.detail: PO gate decision (2026-07-02): the IP Manager tracks all data associated with each IP idea on its route — Founder route: the professor's progress through the Wildfire program; Hackathon route: what was built at the hackathon; Founder Match route: how the match / matched founder is doing. PO: the app's EXISTING founder-tracking system is the framework to reuse/model this on.

decisions.title: Multi-university tenancy — fully isolated organizations
decisions.detail: PO gate decision (2026-07-02, promoted from REC-4): each university is its own organization with its own IP Managers, fully isolated — an IP Manager cannot see other universities' IP, or the other universities at all.

decisions.title: University IP is just an 'idea'
decisions.detail: IP is represented in the app as an idea, not a new object type. 'The research is just an idea in our world. It's not a separate thing. It's just an idea.'

decisions.title: Professor = Founder tag + university-IP-origin analytics tag
decisions.detail: The professor (idea owner) carries the existing Founder role/tag — there is no separate 'professor' role. PO gate decision (2026-07-02): additionally, a special analytics tag marks that this founder originated from a university IP idea. Even though the university owns the IP, the professor owns the idea and leads it.

decisions.title: New IP Manager role
decisions.detail: The person who manages the university's IP gets a new role. Their role title in the app is 'IP Manager' regardless of their university title (VP of research, IP office lead, etc.).

decisions.title: Not hackathon-only
decisions.detail: This is NOT solely for hackathons. Not all university IP is hackathon-appropriate (e.g. a device that makes a heart last longer wouldn't be built at a hackathon). Only a subset of ideas would go to a hackathon.

decisions.title: Private by default, then publish
decisions.detail: Imported IP goes in privately by default. The IP Manager selects some or all and hits publish; publishing sends it out (e.g. to Founder Match), with a separate publish path to a hackathon. This also covers the 'put it on hold and decide later' case — private is the hold state.

decisions.title: Import spreadsheet or add individually
decisions.detail: The IP Manager can import a spreadsheet of IP, or add IP individually with a button. [GAP: exact import/add mechanics not specified — 'however they want to do it'.]

decisions.title: Flag professor involvement per idea
decisions.detail: For each idea the IP Manager flags whether the professor wants to be a day-to-day co-founder OR is just a contact whom whoever takes the idea can reach out to directly. This reflects the two professor profiles.

decisions.title: Founder route reuses the existing process
decisions.detail: On the Founder route the professor is a Founder and runs through the Wildfire process exactly as founders do today; Founder Match brings a co-founder, resulting in two founders in one company, as currently set up.

decisions.title: Hackathon route = pickable idea only (no hackathon-management integration)
decisions.detail: On the Hackathon route the IP becomes a hackathon idea. Hackathon applicants can bring their own idea OR select a university IP idea to work on ('I like that one, I want to work on that one'). PO gate clarification (2026-07-02): this feature only marks/publishes an idea as hackathon-pickable — the separate hackathon-management system being built elsewhere is NOT integrated now; it will be updated later with these learnings (parked dependency).

decisions.title: Do NOT rethink founder role-gating now
decisions.detail: Today the only gated role is Founder (a user can be gated to Founder-only). The PO decided this is not the right time to rethink that gating model — leave it as is for this feature.

dependencies.title: Professor account provisioning
dependencies.detail: Imported professors have no account yet. The PO floated a 'send account information' button but did not specify the mechanism ('I don't know'). Confirm how a professor gets an account and becomes a Founder who can run the process.

dependencies.title: Exact import / add / publish mechanics
dependencies.detail: Spreadsheet import vs individual add, and the publish flow (private -> publish to Founder Match and/or hackathon), are directional only. 'Click a button to put it in or however they want... we have to talk to.' Exact mechanics TBD.

dependencies.detail: A planning-phase flow where the IP Manager is notified/emailed to 'select IP to include in hackathon' (none, some, or all) was described, but the PO wasn't sure it ships immediately ('I don't know if we do this right away or not').

dependencies.title: Kirby's roles & responsibilities in the app
dependencies.detail: The PO has not interviewed Kirby about what her roles and responsibilities in the app will be — only talked to the VP and to Peter. Needs discovery.

dependencies.title: Is VPR a distinct role from IP Manager in the app?
dependencies.detail: RESOLVED at PO gate (2026-07-02): one role — the VPR is merged into the IP Manager; no separate VPR role/tab. Kept here for traceability.

recommendations.title: Professor invite / account-provisioning flow
recommendations.rationale: The transcript imports professors with no account and only floats a 'send account information' button ('I don't know'). Without a concrete invite-to-Founder flow, a professor on the Founder route literally cannot log in or run the Wildfire process, so the MVP would miss its own goal.

recommendations.title: Super Admin provisioning of universities + assigning IP Managers
recommendations.rationale: The master matrix has no IP Manager role and no university-org setup. Someone WFL-side must create each university organization and assign its IP Manager before any IP can be entered — the smallest thing that makes day-one usable.

recommendations.title: Wire the university-IP idea into the existing Idea/Application + Founder Match machinery
recommendations.rationale: The PO says IP 'is just an idea' and that the Founder and Founder-Match routes reuse today's process. To FULLY serve the goal, the imported IP idea must actually connect to the existing idea/company entities and Founder Match rather than be a parallel silo.

recommendations.title: University-IP provenance label + professor contact on the idea
recommendations.rationale: Downstream founder-match users and hackathon participants need to know an idea is university-owned IP and who the professor contact is (especially for contact-only professors). Without provenance the 'reach out directly' path can't work.

recommendations.title: Private-vs-published state + empty state for the IP Manager's list
recommendations.rationale: The private-by-default/publish model needs a clear visible state per idea and a first-run empty state, or an IP Manager opening a fresh, empty list can't tell what's live vs held — the smallest thing that makes the publish model legible.

recommendations.title: Attribution / audit on import, routing, and publish
recommendations.rationale: Recording who imported, routed, and published each piece of IP protects the university relationship and is a cheap addition that a hand-built DoD would likely miss.

recommendations_resolved.title: Multi-university tenancy — each university its own org, IP Manager scoped to it
recommendations_resolved.resolution: ACCEPTED at PO gate (2026-07-02) — promoted to decision 'Multi-university tenancy — fully isolated organizations'.

criteria.criterion: An IP Manager can bring IP into the app (spreadsheet import or individual add) and it lands private by default.
Each imported idea is associated with a professor and carries the professor-involvement flag (co-founder vs contact).
An IP Manager can route each piece of IP down exactly one of the three paths (Founder / Hackathon / Founder Match).
Publishing an idea moves it from private to the selected destination(s); unpublished IP is not visible downstream.

For each routed idea the IP Manager can see its current status on its route — founder-route progress through the Wildfire program, what was built at the hackathon, or how the founder match is doing — using the existing founder-tracking framework.
There is exactly one university-side role (IP Manager) — no separate VPR role or tab.
An IP Manager sees only their own university's organization and IP; other universities and their IP are completely invisible.
A professor who becomes a Founder from a university IP idea carries the special university-IP-origin analytics tag.
All IP data entry happens inside the Wildfire app by a logged-in user — no external data entry.
Existing app behavior (founders, mentors, hackathon roles) is unaffected.
Responsive web, mobile portrait supported. (Template default.)
